title: Rhiya Ahir Pushes Back Against Online Smear Campaign After Iconic CJP Protest Moment
excerpt: The 27-year-old Mumbai model and actress, who went viral for blocking a police van during CJP's anti-NEET protest, has addressed the wave of online abuse and misinformation targeting her since the incident.
body:
• Rhiya Ahir, a 27-year-old Mumbai model and actress, became a protest icon after blocking a police van carrying detained CJP protesters at Shivaji Park on July 23.
  • Since going viral, Ahir has faced online abuse and fabricated claims aimed at discrediting her, which she has publicly rejected as fake and degrading.
  • Her defiant stand — lasting nearly 40 minutes in heavy rain — drew comparisons to the Tiananmen Square 'Tank Man' and became a defining image of the nationwide Cockroach movement.
  • Ahir says she will continue speaking out despite the harassment, calling it a familiar playbook deployed against women in Indian political activism.

A young woman in a grey hoodie, arms spread wide in front of a police van on a rain-soaked Mumbai street, has become one of the most recognisable faces of India's ongoing protest movement — and one of its most targeted. Rhiya Ahir, the 27-year-old model and actress behind the instantly iconic image from July 23, has hit back at what she describes as fake and degrading claims circulating online since the incident went viral.

"I am using my platform and putting myself forward out there, even if people are abusing me and accusing me of different things," Ahir told Careers360, addressing the backlash directly.

The Moment That Went Viral

Ahir was walking from Kohinoor Square in Dadar towards Shivaji Park to join a solidarity protest with the Cockroach Janata Party's nationwide agitation against the NEET paper leak when she spotted a police van filled with detained demonstrators. According to Hindustan Times, she intervened immediately, questioning officers about the reasons for the detentions and whether proper legal procedures had been followed.

https://x.com/gulf_news/status/2080930988792684796

"I couldn't help myself. Their chants — they pulled me towards them. I was like, if I'm going for the protest, it starts from here. They're taking them away, and I cannot let that happen."

— Rhiya Ahir, in an interview with Hindustan Times

When her questions went unanswered, Ahir positioned herself directly in front of the vehicle, preventing it from proceeding. The standoff lasted nearly 40 minutes in heavy rain, according to The Indian EYE, as hundreds of mobile cameras captured the scene. The image drew instant comparisons to the anonymous man who blocked military tanks near Tiananmen Square in 1989.

From Actress to Accidental Activist

Before July 23, Ahir was known as a professional model with nearly one lakh Instagram followers and appearances in music videos, most recently 'Dilbara'. She has performed in theatre since she was four-and-a-half years old.

"Until now, my only 'act' was that of acting, and not activism. I did theatre for 13 years of my life. So, I know how to command the frame. Probably that's what manifested as me standing my ground."

— Rhiya Ahir, speaking to Careers360

She described the confrontation as "an out-of-body experience" that did not feel like extraordinary courage. "People really expect me to say, 'Hey, I was scared,' but I wasn't scared. That's me as a person. That's the way I was raised, to raise my voice." Though she appeared composed, she later admitted to Hindustan Times she was "shaking on the inside."

The Online Backlash

As the videos spread, so did the scrutiny. While supporters hailed Ahir's stand as a powerful expression of civic courage, others questioned her motives, and fabricated claims about her personal life began circulating online. The pattern — a young woman takes a public political stance and is met with character attacks, fake narratives, and gendered abuse — has played out repeatedly in India's digital landscape.

Ahir has refused to retreat. She has continued using her growing platform to advocate for the student movement, urging young people not to wait for the "perfectly Instagrammable aesthetics" before raising their voices. She also directed a pointed message at Prime Minister Narendra Modi: "I actually want to see some resolutions and solutions to the entire problem. Not just words, but also actions and successful implementation."

A Movement's Defining Image

Ahir's act of defiance came amid the CJP-led 'Sansad Chalo' march, part of a nationwide agitation over alleged NEET examination irregularities. Mumbai demonstrators took to the streets on July 23 in solidarity with protests at Jantar Mantar in Delhi, where the CJP demanded the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan. The movement has since produced results: Pradhan resigned, and Pralhad Joshi was appointed as the new Education Minister.

For Ahir, the police are missing an opportunity. "I really feel that they're sleeping on their Singham moment," she quipped, suggesting officers should place themselves "on the right side of history." Her response to the misinformation campaign has been unequivocal: she is not backing down.
nri_angle: Ahir's stand has resonated with Indian-origin communities worldwide, drawing parallels to the Tiananmen Square 'Tank Man' and sparking diaspora conversations about civic courage and the cost of dissent in India.
author: Diaspora Desk
